newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran burns 50 tonnes of narcotics.
newsitem.headline: Iran burns 50 tonnes of narcotics.

text.p: Iran's interior ministry in a ceremony on Tuesday burned 50 tonnes (110,000 lb) of illegal drugs seized last year, Iranian television reported.

In remarks monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, Interior Minister Ali Mohammad Besharati said at the ceremony that about two billion rials ($670,000) had been earmarked this year for the fight against drugs.

Iran lies on a key transit route for drugs being smuggled to Europe via Turkey from Pakistan and Afghanistan, and has imposed stiff punishments against drugs smugglers in a bid to crack down on the narcotics trade.

According to Iranian law, possession of five kg (11 lb) of opium or 30 grams (just over one ounce) of heroin is punishable by death. More than 1,000 people have been executed in drug-related cases since the law took effect in 1989.
Iran said last week it has erected barbed wire fences and hundreds of checkpoints and watchtowers along its borders to prevent traffickers from entering the Islamic republic.
It said that in the Iranian year to March 1997, 175 tonnes (385,800 lb) of various narcotics had been discovered by the Iranian authorities and 16,000 drug dealers arrested.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA said earlier on Tuesday Iranian police had confiscated over one tonne (2,200 lb) of opium from three gangs of drug traffickers in Isfahan.

Provincial intelligence official Mahmoud Shahidi, quoted by IRNA, said 10 vehicles were also confiscated and 20 traffickers were arrested in the raids. He did not say when the seizures had taken place.
Shahidi said provincial law enforcement officials had seized 1,415 kg (3,120 lb) of opium in the past three months from 13 gangs and arrested 59 drug traffickers.
